bib.title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention

question: How can KV cache memory in LLM serving be managed so that fragmentation and duplication stop limiting batch size and throughput?
hypothesis: Managing the KV cache in fixed-size non-contiguous blocks, as OS virtual memory does with pages, gives near-zero waste and lets sequences share blocks, which raises throughput.
contributions: Identify the challenges in memory allocation in serving LLMs and quantify their impact on serving performance.
Propose PagedAttention, an attention algorithm that operates on KV cache stored in non-contiguous paged memory.
Design and implement vLLM, a distributed LLM serving engine built on PagedAttention.
Evaluate vLLM and show it outperforms FasterTransformer and Orca.

method.summary: PagedAttention splits each sequence's KV cache into fixed-size blocks mapped through a per-request block table to physical GPU blocks allocated on demand, with reference counts and copy-on-write for sharing across samples, beams and prefixes. vLLM adds an FCFS scheduler with all-or-nothing preemption (swap to CPU or recompute), Megatron-style tensor parallelism with one shared KV manager, and fused CUDA kernels.

datasets.name: ShareGPT
datasets.size: mean input 161.31 tokens, mean output 337.99 tokens
datasets.preprocessing: tokenized; only input/output lengths used; Poisson arrivals at varied request rates (no timestamps in data)

datasets.name: Alpaca
datasets.size: mean input 19.31 tokens, mean output 58.45 tokens
datasets.source: instruction data generated by GPT-3.5 with self-instruct

datasets.name: WMT16 English-to-German
datasets.preprocessing: two synthesized prefixes: 1-shot (80 tokens) and 5-shot (341 tokens)

other.KV per token: 800 KB (2 x 5120 x 40 x 2 bytes FP16)

models.name: vLLM
models.architecture: serving engine, FastAPI frontend, 8.5K lines Python + 2K lines C++/CUDA, PyTorch, NCCL

models.name: FasterTransformer
models.architecture: latency-optimised inference engine; authors add a custom dynamic-batching scheduler with max batch size B as large as memory allows

models.name: Orca (Max/Pow2/Oracle)
models.architecture: authors' own re-implementation (Orca not public) with buddy allocation; Max reserves 2048 tokens, Pow2 over-reserves outputs by at most 2x, Oracle knows true output length

inference.decoding: basic sampling (1 sample per request) in 6.2; parallel sampling (sizes 2,4,6) and beam search (widths 2,4,6) in 6.3
inference.max_tokens: 2048 (model max); chatbot: prompt cut to last 1024 tokens, at most 1024 generated
inference.samples: 1-hour traces per experiment, 15-minute traces for OPT-175B; number of runs or seeds not stated
inference.prompting: chatbot: chat history + last user query concatenated; KV cache not kept between conversation rounds

parameters.scheduling: FCFS, latest requests preempted first, all-or-nothing eviction, sequence groups gang-scheduled

other.cloud: Google Cloud A2 instances with NVIDIA A100

metrics.name: normalized latency
metrics.definition: mean of every request's end-to-end latency divided by its output length

metrics.name: sustained request rate
metrics.definition: highest request rate before normalized latency explodes (read from curves)

metrics.name: KV memory saving from sharing
metrics.definition: blocks saved by sharing divided by total blocks without sharing

eval.protocol: Request-rate sweeps on synthesized Poisson traces; no repeats, seeds or error bars stated; no accuracy evaluation (outputs are claimed unchanged).

availability.data: ShareGPT, Alpaca, WMT16 are public; synthesized traces not released in the paper

prompts.purpose: shared-prefix example (Fig 10, adopted from GPT-3 paper)
prompts.text: Translate English to French: "sea otter" => "loutre de mer" "peppermint" => "menthe poivrée" "plush girafe" => "girafe en peluche" "cheese" =>

results.claim: vLLM improves serving throughput 2-4x over FasterTransformer and Orca at the same latency.
results.quote: improves the throughput of popular LLMs by 2-4× with the same level

results.claim: Existing systems use only 20.4-38.2% of KV cache memory for token states.
results.setup: Fig 2: authors' Orca (Max/Pow2/Oracle) re-implementations, OPT-13B experiment of 6.2
results.quote: only 20.4% - 38.2% of the KV cache memory is used to store the actual token states

results.claim: vLLM KV cache usage for token states is 96.3% (rest is waste).
results.setup: Fig 2, vLLM bar, same experiment as the Orca bars
results.table: Fig 2 vLLM bar; numbers 20.4, 38.2, 96.3 appear in figure text
results.note: Fig 2 text lists 96.3 for vLLM; mapping of the other values to Orca variants is by figure order

results.claim: On ShareGPT vLLM sustains 1.7-2.7x higher request rates than Orca (Oracle).
On ShareGPT vLLM sustains 2.7-8x higher request rates than Orca (Max).
vLLM sustains up to 22x higher request rates than FasterTransformer.
vLLM batches 2.2x more requests than Orca (Oracle) and 4.3x more than Orca (Max) on OPT-13B ShareGPT.
results.quote: vLLM processes 2.2× more requests at the same time than Orca (Oracle) and 4.3× more

results.claim: Parallel sampling saves 6.1-9.8% KV memory on Alpaca (2-6 samples).
Beam search saves 37.6-55.2% KV memory on Alpaca (widths 2-6).
On ShareGPT, sharing saves 16.2-30.5% (parallel sampling) and 44.3-66.3% (beam search).
results.quote: 16.2% - 30.5% memory saving on parallel sampling and 44.3% - 66.3% on beam search

results.claim: vLLM advantage over Orca (Oracle) grows from 1.3x (basic sampling) to 2.3x (beam width 6).
results.quote: goes from 1.3× in basic sampling to 2.3× in beam search with a width of 6

results.claim: Shared 1-shot prefix: 1.67x throughput over Orca (Oracle).
results.quote: vLLM achieves 1.67× higher throughput than Orca (Oracle)

results.claim: Shared 5-shot prefix: 3.58x throughput over Orca (Oracle).
results.quote: vLLM achieves 3.58× higher throughput than Orca (Oracle)

results.claim: Chatbot workload: vLLM sustains 2x higher request rates than the three Orca baselines.
results.setup: OPT-13B, ShareGPT, prompt cut to last 1024 tokens, max 1024 generated
results.quote: vLLM can sustain 2× higher request rates

results.claim: PagedAttention kernels are 20-26% slower than FasterTransformer's attention kernel.
results.setup: Kernel microbenchmark, Fig 18a, batch sizes 8 and 32

results.claim: Block size 16 is the default; ShareGPT is best at 16-128, Alpaca degrades above 32.
results.setup: Fig 18b, basic sampling, fixed request rates
results.quote: vLLM sets its default block size as 16

results.claim: Recomputation overhead is never higher than 20% of swapping's latency; 16-64 block sizes give comparable end-to-end performance.
results.quote: recomputation overhead is never higher than 20% of swapping’s latency

results.claim: OPT-13B KV cache costs 800 KB per token, up to 1.6 GB per 2048-token request.
results.setup: OPT-13B, FP16: 2 x 5120 x 40 x 2 bytes
results.quote: the KV cache of a single token demands 800 KB of space

results.claim: On a 40GB A100 serving a 13B model, weights take about 65% (26GB) and KV cache over 30%.
Prompt KV cache is 12% of total KV memory in the parallel sampling experiment.
results.quote: accounts for 12% of the total KV cache memory

limits: Orca is not public: all Orca baselines (Max, Pow2, Oracle) are the authors' own re-implementation with an assumed buddy allocator, so the 20-38% usage figure is for these re-implementations, not for production systems.
No repeats, seeds or confidence intervals; no temperature or sampling settings given.
Gains shrink when compute-bound (OPT-175B on Alpaca, Fig 12f).
Authors say the paging idea does not generally apply to DNN training (static shapes) or compute-bound non-LLM serving, where indirection may hurt.
KV cache is not kept across chatbot conversation rounds.
Attention kernel is 20-26% slower than FasterTransformer's.
Evaluated on OPT and LLaMA-13B only, on A100 GPUs; hardware and engine have since moved on (the paper says only that FLOPS grow faster than memory).
